title: Policy Evaluation — Explainability & Runtime Logs (arch notes)
content:
Purpose:
This is an engineering-first sketch of the policy evaluation pipeline internals with emphasis on explainability logs and runtime observability. Primary audience: platform engineers, SREs, and runtime owners who need to instrument, debug, and evolve routing/policy behavior across regions and control planes.

Context / constraints we care about:
- Needs to run in-hosted and private control planes with identical semantics.
- Low-latency on-path evaluation (target < 1.5ms added p95 per request for simple policies).
- Deterministic tie-breaking for routing decisions (important for audits).
- Explainability logs must be compact, replayable, and privacy-safe (strip PII before writing).
- Multi-region: evaluations can be performed locally or via central policy service depending on policy type and trust level (see routing below).

High-level pipeline (runtime path):
1) Request normalization — canonicalize request metadata (model id, customer id, route, sequence length, client tags).
2) Pre-eval enrichment — fetch cached customer config, quota window, and recent latency signals.
3) Constraint stage — boolean checks (hard constraints) evaluated in short-circuit order. If any fail, return explicit deny reason.
4) Scoring stage — numeric scoring functions produce floats for policies that rank routes/models/regions.
5) Tie-break & selection — deterministic stable-sort + fallback rules.
6) Explainability emission — per-decision compact record persisted to explainability store (and sampled to full-trace backends).
7) Post-decision side-effects — metrics, audit log push, optionally persist chosen route for later tracing.

Constraint language (quick sketch):
- Declarative JSON-first grammar used in control plane; compiled to fast eval bytecode at runtime.
- Example constraint snippets (human readable):
  - allow_if: customer.quota.tokens_left > request.estimated_tokens
  - deny_if: request.model.variant == "quantized-8" && customer.sla == "enterprise"
- Operators: exists, in_set, regex_match (avoid heavy regex at p99 path), numeric comparisons.
- Fast-path: compile frequent constraints into a flattened boolean DAG so evaluation is just traversal + memory lookups.
- Edge case: constraints that require historical windows (e.g., error-rate over 5m) are flagged as "stateful" and only evaluated using recent cached aggregates (approx staleness bound documented).

Scoring functions and cost model integration:
- Scorers return a tuple: (score_value: float, explain_tokens: [short tags])
- Default composite scoring = weighted_sum(cost_score, latency_score, freshness_score, sticky_affinity)
- Cost_score derived from model unit cost estimates (token cost + GPU min-cost fraction), normalized per-customer discount tiers.
- Latency_score uses recent p95 latency per region+model; normalized so lower latency -> higher score.
- Freshness_score tracks how recently a model was warmed for that customer (warm caches get boost).
- Sticky_affinity: if customer has previously used a dedicated pool for last N requests, give small preference to avoid cache warmups.
- Scores exposed in explain logs as short tags + numeric values (e.g., "cost":0.37, "latency":0.72).

Explainability logs schema (compact, string-keyed):
- footprint is critical: we store one short record per decision; sampling rate configurable per-customer.
- each record fields (all as strings or short arrays):
  - ts: ISO8601 timestamp
  - req_id: short uuid
  - customer_id
  - policy_id
  - eval_version (policy binary hash)
  - constraints_evaluated: ["c1","c2","c3"] (list of ids)
  - constraints_result: ["pass","fail:quota_low","pass"] (aligned with above list)
  - top_scores: ["r:east-1:0.82","r:west-2:0.71"] (compact route:score strings)
  - selected: "r:east-1"
  - reason: "selected_by_score" or "blocked_by_constraint:quota_low"
  - rule_trace: ["c1:checked","s1:cost=0.37","s2:latency=0.72","tie-break:sticky_affinity"] (short human readable tokens)
  - safe_context_hash: "h:abcd1234" (hash of redacted request context to allow replay joins without PII)
  - trace_ref: optional pointer to full trace in tracing backend (if sampled)

Storage & retention:
- Explain logs go to a fast write path (Kafka-like topic) -> short-term store (30 days hot) -> cold S3 archive (1y by default).
- Hot store is partitioned by customer_id to allow quick lookups. Use compaction keys (policy_id+req_id) to avoid duplicates.
- Retention and sampling configurable per-customer (enterprise customers may require full retention & export).

Observability and debug workflows:
- Alerting rules: constraint-fail-rate spike, frequent policy version flaps, repeated tie-break usage (suggests scoring weights degenerate).
- Live debugging: given req_id, fetch explainability record -> expand trace_ref -> show full scoring breakdown + cached values used.
- For cross-region issues, annotate explain logs with origin_region and effective_evaluation_region so we can detect central-eval-induced latency.

Multi-region considerations and control plane split:
- Two modes: local-eval and central-eval.
  - Local-eval: policy binaries + cached aggregates deployed to region; best latency, eventual consistency for stateful constraints.
  - Central-eval: single control plane evaluates authoritative decision; stronger consistency but higher latency and network dependency.
- Heuristic for mode selection: prefer local-eval if constraints are stateless or use coarse aggregates; prefer central-eval for audit-critical or config-change operations.
- Deployment: policy binary + evaluator runtime version pinned per-region. Announce policy changes via config-version in explain logs to aid postmortems.

Determinism and auditability:
- Deterministic execution order: constraints and scorers have declared priorities and a stable sort key. Evaluation engine must produce identical selection given same inputs and binary hash.
- Policy binary hash included in every explain record (eval_version) for later repro.
- Replay tool: support offline replay using explain logs + safe_context_hash to reproduce decision and verify that different runtime versions would have produced same result.

Performance & micro-optimizations:
- Pre-allocate scratch buffer per thread to avoid allocations during scoring.
- Inline common cost lookups with L1 cache in region process; fallback to async cache miss path to avoid blocking.
- Short-circuit constraints early: rank by expected likely-fail probability (learned from historical explain logs) so we bail fast on common deny reasons.
- JIT compile hot scorers to native code if observed > 1k evals/sec in a region (experimental).

Security & privacy:
- Strip any user-provided text or PII before emitting explain logs.
- safe_context_hash must be irreversible on server unless customer provides decryption key (enterprise feature).
- Access to full traces gated by RBAC and logged.

Operational runbook snippets (for SREs):
- On spike of constraint failures: check recent policy deployments, compare eval_version from explain logs to expected, run replay on a sample of failed req_ids.
- On unexpected tie-breaks: surface scoring component distributions from explain logs (histogram of cost vs latency score). If degenerate, tweak weights and roll out canary.
- Cross-region latency increase: check if eval_mode switched to central-eval (explain logs have effective_evaluation_region). If yes, consider fail-open local-eval policy until control-plane backpressure resolved.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Finalize compact serialization format for explainability records (we currently use JSON; need smaller binary proto for high-volume customers).
- Formal grammar for the constraint language and type system; design static analyzer so we can catch vacuous constraints at compile time.
- Backfill: how to attach model runtime metrics (cache hit/miss) to individual explain records without blowing up record size.
- Sampling strategy: dynamic sampling that preserves at-least-N per-customer per-hour for debugging.

Appendix: sample minimal explain log (single-line JSON for readability)
{"ts":"2026-02-15T14:22:31Z","req_id":"r-6f4b","customer_id":"cust-1023","policy_id":"route-v2","eval_version":"h1a2b3","constraints_evaluated":["c_quota","c_region_allowed"],"constraints_result":["pass","fail:region_blocked"],"top_scores":["r:us-east-1:0.83","r:eu-west-1:0.60"],"selected":null,"reason":"blocked_by_constraint:region_blocked","rule_trace":["c_quota:ok","c_region_allowed:fail"]}
Notes: this doc is a working draft. I expect to split into two follow-ups: (1) explainability log schema RFC (binary proto + retention policy), (2) runtime evaluator performance micro-PRs.
